biodiversity_overview.text: 36,831 GBIF occurrence records for 75 tracked species are attributed to Telangana, spanning 1876-2026.
36,041 of these records (97.9%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 28, Magnoliopsida 15, Mammalia 15, Squamata 5, Testudines 4, Actinopterygii 4, Amphibia 3, Crocodylia 1.

threatened_species.text: 8 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Mugger Crocodile (VU), Sloth Bear (VU), Asian Elephant (EN), Tiger (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: White-throated Munia (4,263), Indian Robin (2,926), Indian Pied Starling (2,791), Indian Spot-billed Duck (2,611), Common Peafowl (2,288).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 3,049 in 2016 to 690 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 5.97% of Telangana's area (16 areas intersect the state).
13.8% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (4,964 of 36,041); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Narrow-headed Softshell Turtle (0.54), Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Indian Courser (0.47), Mugger Crocodile (0.46).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Telangana (equal-weight reference): cell near 17.625N 78.375E (overall rank 55, median rank across weightings 74); cell near 18.375N 79.125E (overall rank 83, median rank across weightings 111); cell near 16.875N 79.875E (overall rank 116, median rank across weightings 135).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 5,350 km2 (4.82% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

382.2 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (7.14% of the 2000 extent; 0.69% in 2015-2024, rank 17 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2011 (65.18 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.03% of land and population density is 350.9 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
31% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
